newsitem.title: UK: North Sea spreads, CFDs slightly up in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: North Sea spreads, CFDs slightly up in quiet market.

text.p: North Sea intermonth spreads and contracts for differences tightened slightly in a quiet market on Monday, traders said.
The Brent cash market rose in early trade, with June Brent 21 cents a barrel up at $18.13 by 1054 GMT.
Traders said the North Sea physical market was quiet with no cargoes changing hands early on Monday, but both intermonth spreads and CFDs firmed.
May/June firmed by two cents to -20 cents, while June/July fetched -11 cents.
CFDs also rose with next week's trading at June Brent -44 cents, or 64 cents above Dated Brent, while May 5-9 was at June Brent -39 cents.

Traders said the North Sea crude market could get a shot in the arm from the opportunity to substitute for West African barrels in the U.S. Gulf, as millions of barrels of Nigerian and other West African grades were heading to Asia.
In a quiet Mediterranean market, Russian Urals were a little weaker than last week's levels, being talked at about Dated Brent -$1.20.
"I haven't heard of any deals today...It (Urals) seems slightly weaker when people start indicating their May cargoes. The pressure is coming from the cheaper Kirkuk," one trader said.
Negotiations between Syrian state oil company Sytrol and term lifters over May term prices are expected to end later this weak, traders said.
They said the Syrians were still clinging to their offer of Dated Brent -82 cents while buyers were hoping for something in the mid-80s range.
